text: The night was warm. The gum trees stood so tall.
Sunny wandered where the moonlight softly fell.
High in a fork of silver-branching leaves,
a round grey shape sat sleepy in the tree.
A little koala, fluffy, soft, and round,
with big round ears and a shiny button nose.
He hugged the trunk with soft and sleepy paws,
his eyes half-closed against the gentle dark.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “Are you off to sleep?”
“Almost,” he yawned. “I sleep the whole day long.”
He nibbled one last gum leaf, slow and calm,
then settled deeper in his cosy tree.
“I rest and rest,” the koala softly said.
“There's nothing nicer than a good long snooze.”
So Sunny breathed the sweet warm gum-leaf air
and felt how good it was to slow right down.
The koala's eyes grew heavy, drooping low,
his fluffy head a-nod against the bark.
He tucked his paws and curled into a ball,
snug and safe up in his gum-tree bed.
Sunny found a hollow, soft with leaves,
and nestled down beneath the sleeping tree.
The bush was still. The moon was climbing slow.
Everything was peaceful, warm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy as the gum leaves swayed.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept as soundly as the koala,
both of them dreaming in the quiet night.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, sleepy koala.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
